title: Budget vs Revenue
text:
This page will explore the relationship between budgets and revenues for well-known box office films. Based on the scatterplot Figure 1, we can see that there is a positive correlation between large budgets and large revenue.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget (millions of USD)")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (millions of USD)")
plt.title("Budget vs Revenue")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Budgets vs. Revenues

title: Movies
text:
This dataset explores some of the biggest box-office hit movies in history. It includes information on the year it was released, franchise, the film’s budget, the film’s revenue, the length of the film, as well as its public rating on IMDB. There is further analysis on the relationship between a film’s budget and revenue, a film’s runtime and rating, and the revenue of the Bond films.
For this assignment, I utilized no AI.

title: Runtime vs Rating
text:
This page will explore the relationship between runtime and ratings for well-known box office films. Based on the scatterplot Figure 1, we can see that there is a weak correlation between longer runtime and higher ratings.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDB Rating (0 to 10)")
plt.title("Runtime vs Rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Runtime vs. Ratings

title: The Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (millions of USD)")
plt.title("Bond Films Revenue over Time")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Bond Revenue over Time





The first Bond year was 1995 and the last Bond year was 2021.
